title: Vida
game_overview: An artificial life evolution simulator where hinged rectangular organisms navigate water physics and evolve swimming locomotion through neural networks and natural selection.
winning_condition: Endless open-ended sandbox simulation with no win condition; observe continuous multi-generational evolution and adaptation indefinitely.
losing_condition: All creatures and incubating eggs perish, causing total population extinction.

controls.action: Pan camera across the aquatic tank.
Select organism to inspect anatomy, neural network, energy, and lineage.
Spawn manual nutrient burst at cursor location.
On-screen buttons for simulation speed, inspection, spawning food, and camera recenter.

sections.title: Design Pillars
sections.content: 1. True Emergent Locomotion: No predetermined or hardcoded swimming formulas; propulsion emerges purely from joint torque motors reacting to hydrodynamic drag forces. 2. Minimalist Elegance: Clean high-contrast vector aesthetic with luminous bioluminescent creature accents against a deep abyss tank. 3. Computational High Performance: Optimized spatial hashing and lightweight feedforward neural nets supporting hundreds of active articulated bodies simultaneously.
sections.summary: Core foundational philosophies of the ecosystem simulator.

sections.title: Core Loop
sections.content: The simulation initializes with random primordial organisms composed of linked rectangular segments in a vast aquatic reservoir. Organisms fire neural motor outputs into joint hinges, causing body oscillations. Forward hydrodynamic drag pushes successful swimmers toward nutrient particles. Consuming nutrients restores energy and increases maturity. Organisms with sufficient energy lay eggs containing mutated genomes (morphology, segment dimensions, and neural connection weights). Starving or aged organisms expire and dissolve into ambient nutrients. Natural selection autonomously filters ineffective morphologies while compounding viable propulsion strategies over dozens of generations.
sections.summary: The generational cycle of survival, feeding, reproduction, and selection.

sections.title: Core Mechanics
sections.content: 1. Hydrodynamic Ragdoll Physics: Each creature consists of 2 to 6 rectangular rigid segments connected via angular hinge joints. Fluid physics calculates normal and tangential drag per segment, converting oscillating flukes and fin motions into forward thrust. 2. Neural Architecture & Sensory Perception: Lightweight feedforward perceptron networks receive color-spectrum raycasts (detecting nutrient vs creature colors), joint angle encoders, angular velocity, and internal energy reserves. Outputs command target joint angular velocities. 3. Genetic Mutation & Reproduction: When reaching maturity (>80% energy), creatures lay physical buoyant eggs. Offspring inherit genome with stochastic mutations (joint limits, segment lengths, weight perturbations, and topological additions). 4. Environmental Nutrients: Organic algae nutrients drift through the water column with subtle convection currents, auto-replenishing to maintain ecological equilibrium.
sections.summary: Physics, neural networks, genetics, and metabolic systems.

sections.title: Movement & Scrolling Alignment
sections.content: Scrolling Axis: Multi-Directional free-roaming aquatic tank. Asset Orientation: Creatures align dynamically along their heading vector with zero-radian baseline parallel to the X-axis (facing 3 o'clock). Movement Physics: Realistic simulated fluid dynamics with linear and quadratic fluid resistance, rotational damping, momentum conservation, and elastic soft collisions. Camera Behavior: Smooth interpolated pan-and-zoom viewport with auto-tracking mode for selected specimen.
sections.summary: Free-roaming multi-directional simulation view and fluid kinetics.

sections.title: Visual Hierarchy & Layering
sections.content: Layer Separation: Deep navy-indigo aquatic background with soft ambient caustics and subtle grid coordinates. Playfield entities feature vivid neon bioluminescent pigments (Emerald nutrients, Cyan/Coral/Gold creature segments with glowing joint nodes). Obstacle & Hazard Affordance: Low-energy starving creatures visually desaturate and flicker; gravid egg-bearing specimens pulse with radiant core luminance. HUD Overlay: Sleek glassmorphic telemetry dashboard displaying population graphs, generation counters, speed multipliers, and detailed neural inspector overlay.
sections.summary: Minimalist vector contrast and vital HUD overlays.

sections.title: Characters & Enemies
sections.content: Organisms evolve into diverse emergent archetypes: 1. Flagellates: Long multi-segment undulating eel-like swimmers. 2. Flappers: Compact dual-fin paddlers generating sudden burst propulsion. 3. Gliders: Wide hydrofoil segments minimizing drag for efficient cruising. 4. Filter Feeders: Multi-jointed sweeping bodies that engulf wide particle swathes.

sections.title: Fairness Tools
sections.content: Real-time population graph (living count, average lifespan, generation depth, average velocity), specimen neural visualizer showing active synapse firings, manual nutrient dispenser, and time acceleration up to 10x.
sections.summary: Analytical and observational tools for player experimentation.

sections.title: Juice & Game Feel
sections.content: Anticipation Juice: Glowing egg gestational pulse before hatching. State Change Juice: Soft fluid cavitation bubbles emitted during high-velocity joint strokes; gentle shimmering ripples when feeding. Impact Juice: Tactile particle burst upon egg emergence and nutrient absorption, accompanied by soft aquatic audio resonances.

sections.title: Social Mechanics & Audience
sections.content: Designed for artificial life researchers, computational biology fans, and sandbox simulation enthusiasts.

sections.title: Accessibility
sections.content: High-contrast color modes for neural raycasts, pause-and-inspect capability at any simulation step, and flexible UI scaling.

sections.title: Structural Integrity
sections.content: Persistent local storage for ecosystem state, pre-baked primordial soup presets (Standard, High Turbulence, Dense Nutrients), and instant ecosystem reset.
sections.summary: Save states, presets, and ecosystem management flow.

sections.title: Virtual Touch Controls Implementation
sections.content: Render on-screen virtual floating control bar when mobile is detected using useIsMobile(). Buttons include Play/Pause, Speed 1x/2x/5x, Spawn Food, Specimen Tracking Toggle, and Reset. Wire up onPointerDown and onPointerUp with pointer-events-auto exclusively on buttons and touch-none class to prevent default scrolling.
